newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA NHAVA PORT BEGINS WORK ON CONTAINER TERMINAL.
newsitem.headline: INDIA NHAVA PORT BEGINS WORK ON CONTAINER TERMINAL.

text.p: Nhava Sheva International Container Terminal Ltd, which recently won a licence to build and operate a container terminal on the western Indian coast, said it began work on the $200 million project.
The company said in a statement on Tuesday it has placed the first order for container handling equipment with the German engineering firm Preussag Noell AG, a unit of Preussag AG.

"They (the equipment ordered) will offer performance levels well above those prescribed by the licensor agency Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust, and will set new benchmarks for port efficiency in India," the statement said.
"For users, this will mean much shorter turnaround times and faster throughput, both serious problems at most Indian ports."

Nhava Sheva International Container Terminal Ltd is a joint venture between P&O Australia Ports Pty Ltd --a unit of the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co --, Konsortium Perkapalan Berhard of Malaysia and DBC Port Management Pvt Ltd, an Indian stevedoring company.

The company plans to build a 600 metre container terminal within the Jawaharlal Nehru Port on the western Maharashtra coast which, when fully built, will have a capacity to handle upto 600,000 twenty-foot containers per annum.
The terminal will be built in two phases, with the first phase scheduled to be completed by end 1998.
